channel.title: Multi-tenant :: Juice's documentation
channel.description: MultiTenant This core feature is useful to verify other core features that we have built because it is developed as a microservice. It’s integrated with Finbuckle to identity the tenant. We provide multiple choices for tenant data store: File store EFCore store gRPC store We also provide the gRPC API to manage tenant information and tenant settings, so MultiTenant itself is a service with the full implementation of: MultiTenant DBContext UnitOfWork pattern Audit gRPC API DDD/CQRS and Domain Events pattern Integration with event bus Per-tenant configuration/options xUnit helper To use multi-tenant, we must register services with Tenant type

item.title: Tenant pattern (decision record)
item.description: Status: Accepted, 24 November 2026. Applies to: the Juice framework (Juice.Extensions.MultiTenant, Juice.EF.MultiTenant), juice-tenants (services/multitenant), and every service built on Juice (Juice.Observability, Juice.Notifications, the services under services/). Context Juice services identify tenants in three different ways today. How the request’s tenant is found Key used Checks the tenant exists and is active Juice framework and juice-tenants Finbuckle strategies: base path, header, route, per-tenant OIDC login The Identifier (the tenant’s name in URLs). The gRPC __tenant__ header carries the Identifier too Yes, through the tenant store Juice.Observability Each deployment serves one fixed tenant (JUICE_PLATFORM_TENANT_ID); the token’s platform_tenant claim must equal it The Id Its own platform_tenants table, provisioned at install Juice.Notifications The /tenants/{tenantId} route, which must match the token’s platform_tenant claim (TenantAccess) The Id (a GUID) No; only “is this application registered for the tenant” The differences cost us:
